newsitem.title: UK: British Gas says output at Morecambe halted again.
newsitem.headline: British Gas says output at Morecambe halted again.

text.p: British Gas Plc has halted production at its giant Morecambe Bay field after output resumed for less than a week following a three-month shutdown for operational maintenance, a spokesman for British Gas Trading said on Thursday.
British Gas briefly opened the taps at the field last Thursday following the summer closure to meet a rise in gas demand, he added.
"This was a temporary measure and production has been stopped for the moment," he told Reuters.
The spokesman did not say when production would resume.
"One of the big advantages Morecambe gives us is a big swing capacity," he said. "If we need to switch it on we do, if we don't, we don't."
U.K. gas industry regulator Ofgas said on Monday that it was looking into rumours that British Gas had deliberately cut production at its Morecambe field to push spot market prices higher.
But a spokesman at British Gas denied accusations of price manipulation.
"We defend our position very strongly," he said. "The field was closed purely for operational reasons."
"Certainly prices have climbed, but there is still plenty of gas around," he added.
Spot gas prices peaked in mid-September at just over 17 pence a therm for delivery early next year from around 14 pence in early June.
Prices for the same period are now around 16 pence a therm.
The north and south Morecambe fields in the Irish Sea have a production capacity of more than 1.9 billion cubic feet per day, or nearly 16 percent of total U.K. gas output.
